posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Thunderstruck says that a non-character target hit by it loses its end-of-turn text.

I had a game against Gloomweaver and the Cursed Acolyte hit Dynamic Syphon on XPW Tempest, so I hit the Acolyte with Thunderstruck... and the Acolyte continued to hit everyone for damage.

Shouldn't it have stopped?

posts.name: RySmith6
posts.cooked:
Yes, but that text doesn't have to exist anymore. That text triggers the damage action. The damage action is currently happening, not the EOT effect. The EOT effect is "over" when the damage starts. If there was something that were to happen after the damage is done, in the same EOT block, that secondary effect shouldn't happen, but that's not represented here.

[End of Turn:Start Damage action] => (Damage:Do some damage)

Stopping anywhere after here    ^^ won't stop anything outside of the []

posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
mwc146:

The text of the power says the target "loses any "End of Turn" effects on its card."

That, to me, seems like it would mean that once it takes the damage, you treat the card as if that text doesn't exist, whether it was in the middle of that action or not.

Admittedly, I don't think there is a lot of precedent in Sentinels (barring some weird example of somehow getting Sub-Zero Atmosphere out mid-villain-turn), but at the very least, this doesn't sound like a bug to me, just a rule-interpretation dispute.

That said–the reason that we're reading this as we are is a function of being used to the "trigger and resolve" style that most games operate on; once the trigger is hit, the card is resolving it–too late to remove the text.
